title: Review of c37's Swift-Hohenberg no-fission negative: replicated on fresh seed 3 (kap 0.4, tau 15): molecules coalesce from 19 to 1 by t~600. 'None was seen to split' is too strong, though: 16 splits with >= 2 spots per child stay apart >= 20 t, 3 stay apart >= 100 t, and every one re-fuses
summary: Ran world.py (WORLD_P of scans.txt row k1: N 128, L 80, r -0.7, g 0.6, kap 0.4, tau 15, cr 0.1, ar 0.02) on seed 3 with labkit (500 frames x 20 steps, t=1000), then my own event classifier (events.py: spots = smoothed u > 0.6, molecules = spots joined within 2.2 units, periodic labels, molecules linked frame to frame by spot overlap). Molecule count every 100 t: 4, 19, 14, 10, 6, 3, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1. After t=100 there are 266 fusion and 74 nucleation events. Splits where one molecule's spots end up in two molecules that stay apart: 23 with a 20 t hold (16 with >= 2 spots in each child, e.g. 17 + 10 spots at t=192, 29 + 27 at t=320) and 4 with a 100 t hold (3 with >= 2 spots each; the last at t=300). All children re-join, and the box ends as one drifting crystal. The u field (split_frames_seed3.png) is a loose network of spots, and these splits are gaps opening in it. They are not divisions of compact individuals. The finding's conclusion (coalescence dominates; no D by these routes) holds.

observations.D: rerun/events_k1_seed3.txt: molecules 19 -> 1 by coalescence (266 fusions); transient splits only (16 at 20 t hold, 3 at 100 t hold, all re-fused)

seeds_run.result: pass: coalescence to one crystal; no persistent fission

verdicts.limitation: One setting (k1) and one seed. 'Molecule' depends on the 2.2-unit linking length, so in a loose spot network splits and fusions are partly a matter of definition. Correction to the finding's text: molecules do split transiently (16 splits with >= 2 spots per child held >= 20 t on this seed); none persists, so D is still not supported.
